sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: (a) Which d-block element has the minimum oxidation state of +2 only? (b) Name the alloy of copper and zinc.
State true or false: (a) Transition metal ions with unpaired electrons are generally coloured. (b) Zn^2+ is coloured as it has a completely filled d subshell.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – a completely filled d¹⁰ configuration has no d–d transition, so it is colourless.

questions.q: Fill in: (a) The 3d series starts with ______. (b) The lanthanoid contraction is caused by the poor shielding of ______ electrons.
Write (a) the chief ore of chromium and (b) the colour of the dichromate ion.
Match: (a) K2Cr2O7 (b) KMnO4 (c) Brass with (i) purple (ii) Cu + Zn (iii) orange.
Write (a) the electronic configuration of Cu (Z = 29) and (b) the oxidation states of Mn in KMnO4.
(a) What is an alloy? (b) Give one use of steel.
questions.answer: (a) A homogeneous mixture of a metal with other metals or non-metals. (b) Used for building structures, tools and machinery.

questions.q: Complete: (a) Actinoids are ______ elements. (b) Cerium commonly shows the oxidation state +3 and ______.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why are transition metals and their compounds often coloured?
questions.answer: The partially filled d orbitals split in energy in the presence of ligands, and electrons absorb visible light for d–d transitions; the transmitted complementary colour is observed.

questions.q: What are alloys? Give the composition and one use of brass.
questions.answer: Alloys are homogeneous mixtures of metals with other metals or non-metals. Brass = copper + zinc; used for making utensils, musical instruments and decorative items.

questions.q: What is lanthanoid contraction? State one consequence.
questions.answer: The regular decrease in atomic and ionic radii of lanthanoids with increasing atomic number because 4f electrons shield the nuclear charge poorly. Consequence: Zr and Hf have almost identical radii and properties, and are difficult to separate.

questions.q: Why do transition elements have high melting points and densities?
questions.answer: Strong metallic bonding by a large number of unpaired d electrons and small atomic size gives high melting points and close-packed structures with high density.

questions.q: Why do transition metals show variable oxidation states?
questions.answer: The (n−1)d and ns electrons have nearly the same energy and can both take part in bonding; the oxidation states differ by one unit (Mn: +2 to +7).

questions.q: Write the reaction of acidified potassium permanganate with Fe^2+ ions.
questions.answer: MnO4− + 8H+ + 5Fe^2+ → Mn^2+ + 4H2O + 5Fe^3+ (purple colour changes to almost colourless).

questions.q: Why is Zn not considered a transition element?
questions.answer: Zn^2+ has a completely filled d¹⁰ subshell; it has no incomplete d subshell in its atom or its common ion.

questions.q: Why are Sc^3+ and Cu^+ colourless?
questions.answer: Sc^3+ is d⁰ and Cu^+ is d¹⁰, so neither has a d–d transition.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the general characteristics of transition elements: variable oxidation states, catalytic properties and complex formation.
questions.answer: Variable oxidation states because (n−1)d and ns electrons both take part; catalytic activity due to variable oxidation states and the surface available for adsorption (Fe in Haber, V2O5 in Contact process); complex formation because of small size, high charge and vacant d orbitals.

questions.q: Write the steps in the manufacture of K2Cr2O7 from chromite ore.
questions.answer: 1. Chromite is fused with Na2CO3 in air: 4FeCr2O4 + 8Na2CO3 + 7O2 → 8Na2CrO4 + 2Fe2O3 + 8CO2. 2. Sodium chromate is acidified with H2SO4: 2Na2CrO4 + H2SO4 → Na2Cr2O7 + Na2SO4 + H2O. 3. Treating with KCl: Na2Cr2O7 + 2KCl → K2Cr2O7 + 2NaCl; the orange crystals separate.

questions.q: Write the oxidising action of K2Cr2O7 in acidic medium on (a) Fe^2+ (b) I−.
Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Fe^3+ (Z = 26) and Cu^2+ (Z = 29).
Compare lanthanoids and actinoids (three points).
questions.answer: Lanthanoids fill 4f, actinoids 5f; lanthanoids mainly +3 while actinoids show +3 to +7; lanthanoids are non-radioactive (except Pm) while all actinoids are radioactive.

questions.q: Explain the interconversion of chromate and dichromate with pH.
questions.answer: In acidic solution (low pH), orange Cr2O7^2− is formed: 2CrO4^2− + 2H+ ⇌ Cr2O7^2− + H2O; in alkaline solution (high pH), yellow CrO4^2− is formed.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Describe the manufacture of potassium dichromate from chromite ore. (b) Write the IUPAC-style oxidation states of chromium and write the structure features of the dichromate ion. (c) Give two oxidising reactions of acidified K2Cr2O7.
questions.answer:
(a) Fusion of chromite with soda ash in air gives Na2CrO4; acidification gives Na2Cr2O7, which on treatment with KCl gives K2Cr2O7 (4FeCr2O4 + 8Na2CO3 + 7O2 → 8Na2CrO4 + 2Fe2O3 + 8CO2; 2Na2CrO4 + 2H+ → Na2Cr2O7 + 2Na+ + H2O; Na2Cr2O7 + 2KCl → K2Cr2O7 + 2NaCl).
(b) Cr is +6; Cr2O7^2− has two tetrahedral CrO4 units sharing an oxygen (Cr–O–Cr bridge).
(c) 6Fe^2+ + Cr2O7^2− + 14H+ → 6Fe^3+ + 2Cr^3+ + 7H2O; 3SO2 + Cr2O7^2− + 2H+ → 3SO4^2− + 2Cr^3+ + H2O.

questions.q: (a) What are transition elements? Why are Zn, Cd and Hg not considered transition elements? (b) Explain the formation of coloured ions and paramagnetism.
questions.answer:
(a) Elements with an incomplete d subshell in the atom or ions. Zn, Cd and Hg have d¹⁰ in the atom and in their +2 ions.
(b) In an ion with partially filled d orbitals, d–d transition absorbs visible light, producing colour (Cu^2+ blue, Ni^2+ green). Unpaired electrons give paramagnetism with μ = √[n(n+2)] BM.

questions.q: (a) State the electronic configuration of lanthanoids and the oxidation states. (b) Explain lanthanoid contraction with its causes and consequences. (c) Name two uses of lanthanoids.
questions.answer:
(a) [Xe] 4f¹⁻¹⁴ 5d⁰⁻¹ 6s²; +3 common, Ce +4, Eu +2.
(b) Decrease in atomic and ionic size from La to Lu due to poor shielding by 4f electrons: the effective nuclear charge rises. Consequences: similarity of 4d and 5d elements (Zr–Hf), difficult separation, decrease in basicity of hydroxides.
(c) Misch metal in alloys for lighter flints; cerium compounds in glass polishing.

questions.q: (a) Describe the preparation of KMnO4 from MnO2. (b) Explain its oxidising action in acidic and alkaline medium with equations. (c) State its use.
questions.answer:
(a) MnO2 fused with KOH in air gives green K2MnO4 (2MnO2 + 4KOH + O2 → 2K2MnO4 + 2H2O), which is oxidised by electrolysis or Cl2/ozone to purple KMnO4.
(b) Acidic: MnO4− + 8H+ + 5e− → Mn^2+ + 4H2O. Neutral or alkaline: MnO4− + 2H2O + 3e− → MnO2 + 4OH−.
(c) Used as an oxidising agent in titrations and as a disinfectant (Condy's crystals).
